Vue Integration with

integrates with Vue through . The package preserves the core contract and adds useReactiveState() for reactive State access within a Vue effect scope.

Vue package usage

can run in a Vue application without . The core APIs remain available, but the Vue reactive State surface is supplied only by the Vue package.

Vue Integration

is a Vue integration wrapper around the core APIs. It preserves the core FluentApi, synchronous State Snapshot, and State Stream while adding useReactiveState() as the Vue reactive State surface.

Call useReactiveState() during component setup or within another active Vue effect scope. The effect scope owns the resulting subscription lifecycle and exposes subsequent State changes through the readonly reactive Snapshot, so the component does not require a separate state$ subscription or manual subscription cleanup.

Initial State requires a reactive connection

A manual state$ subscription created after the has initialized can miss the emission that committed the initial State. Later State updates may still reach that subscription even though the component did not receive the current Snapshot during setup.

useReactiveState() gives the component the current Snapshot and connects it to subsequent State changes through the same effect-scope contract. Outside an active effect scope, read state for the latest synchronous Snapshot or use state$ when an explicitly managed Observable subscription is required.

Installation

The Vue extension is available from the package on npm. 

{{`npm install @sdux-vault/vue`}}

Vue Component Pattern

Create and initialize the outside the component, then import its stable reference into the Vue component. During setup, call useReactiveState() once and render from the returned readonly reactive Snapshot. 

{{`import { FeatureCell, Vault } from '@sdux-vault/vue';

Vault({
  logLevel: 'off',
  devMode: false
});

export const counterCell = FeatureCell<number>({
  key: 'counter',
  initialState: 0
});

counterCell.initialize();`}}
 
{{`<script setup lang="ts">
import { counterCell } from './counter.cell';

const snapshot = counterCell.useReactiveState();
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="snapshot.isLoading">Loading...</p>
  <p
    v-else-if="snapshot.error"
    role="alert"
    v-text="snapshot.error.message">
  </p>
  <p v-else-if="!snapshot.hasValue">No State is available.</p>
  <p v-else v-text="'Count: ' + snapshot.value"></p>
</template>`}}
useReactiveState()

useReactiveState() connects the active Vue effect scope to State and returns the latest committed Snapshot as a readonly reactive object. Its value, hasValue, isLoading, and error fields remain reactive as State changes.
